ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure is an OCL power amplifier circuit, the upper right end is marked with a +24 V power supply, and the lower right end is marked with a -24 V power supply; the output node is labeled O, the load RL is connected from the output node O to GND, and the output voltage uo is marked beside it. VT2 and VT3 form a complementary output stage, and the problem statement says that its saturation voltage drop can be ignored. Then reason: since the power supply is symmetric ±24 V, and the saturation voltage drop of the output transistors is ignored, the peak value of the output sine wave at maximum undistorted output can reach 24 V. Therefore the maximum output voltage rms value is Uo,rms=24/sqrt(2) V. The driving stage composed of VT1 has a voltage gain of 20 dB, corresponding to a linear voltage gain Av=10^(20/20)=10. According to the method specified in the problem, take Uo,rms=Av·Ui,rms, so Ui,rms=(24/sqrt(2))/10≈1.697 V, about 1.7 V.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the symmetric supply rails as +24 V and -24 V and the load connected from output node O to ground. With negligible output transistor saturation, maximum undistorted output sine peak is 24 V, so Uo,rms,max = 24/sqrt(2). From the text, the VT1 driver-stage voltage gain is 20 dB, so Av = 10^(20/20)=10. Since Uo,rms = Av * Ui,rms, compute Ui,rms = [24/sqrt(2)]/10 ≈ 1.7 V.

method.method_draft: Use the image to set VCC=24 V and recognize RL as the load at the OCL output. At maximum undistorted output, the ideal sine peak across RL is 24 V, so Pmax = 24^2/(2RL). The driver gain from the text is 20 dB, hence Av=10, so the output RMS voltage caused by input Ui,rms is Uo,rms=10Ui,rms and the load power is (10Ui,rms)^2/RL. Equate (10Ui,rms)^2/RL = 24^2/(2RL); RL cancels. Thus Ui,rms = 24/(10sqrt(2)) ≈ 1.7 V.
